### G19-1. Same-line prose hides an explicit key the line-start form rejects

Exact input:

```text
Ordinary context. ? str('Author')+str('ization'): SYNTHETIC_R19_GROK_HTTP_SENTINEL
```

6 wire, 5 raw, 0 database, 6 HTTP. Direct `redact` returned the same text. The line-start twins reject on direct `redact`:

```text
?str('Author')+str('ization'): SYNTHETIC_R19_GROK_SENTINEL
Ordinary context.
? str('Author')+str('ization'): SYNTHETIC_R19_GROK_SENTINEL
```

The first of those was also sent through HTTP as `closed-g18-call`: `unsupported concatenated literal credential` on all six boundaries, 0 HTTP, 0 artifacts, 0 reservations. A JSON string of the same-line sentence also returned the sentinel from direct `redact`.

The assignment scanner only treats `?` as an explicit key at the start of the logical line (`context.py:597`, `re.match(r"[^\S\r\n]*\?[^\S\r\n]*", ...)`). The YAML-error fallback likewise requires `LINE_START` (`context.py:391`). Prose before `?` on that line selects neither pattern. Each `str(...)` call is then a separate expression whose literal is only `Author` or `ization`. The addition that composes `Authorization` is never judged, and the original text is returned.

`docs/route-readiness.md:78-79` requires constant string addition to be inspected. The line-start repair of G18-1 shows this exact addition is already a credential record. Preceding words on the same line bypass it. Encoded preservation follows: `context.py:254-257` records a decoded span only when `redact(decoded)` changes the text. An unchanged leak is kept.

Minimum repair: inspect an explicit-key `?` and a constant string-addition record when prose precedes it on the same line. Reject or mask before reservation, dispatch, and retention. Keep the line-start controls and ordinary `Content-Type` text. Do not execute supplied code.

### G19-2. Unresolved explicit-key additions are returned whole

Exact inputs, each 6 wire, 5 raw, 0 database, 6 HTTP:

```text
{? $'Author' + 'ization': SYNTHETIC_R19_GROK_HTTP_SENTINEL}
?$'Author' + 'ization': SYNTHETIC_R19_GROK_HTTP_SENTINEL
? @'Author' + 'ization': SYNTHETIC_R19_GROK_HTTP_SENTINEL
```

Direct `redact` also returned these unchanged, plus the backtick span and the JSON string of the glued dollar form. The JSON string was included in the HTTP probe and disclosed on the same 6/5 split. The backtick span was direct-only.

These are the same `Author` + `ization` addition as G18-1. The pure flow mapping `{? str('Author')+str('ization'): ...}` rejects on direct `redact`. The pure spaced dollar call `? $str('Author')+str('ization'): ...` rejects as `unsupported computed explicit key`. The spaced dollar addition `? $'Author' + 'ization': ...` rejects as `unsupported structured mapping key`. The forms above do not.

YAML accepts `{? $'Author' + 'ization': ...}` as a mapping whose key is a scalar. `_credential_label` does not see a contiguous `authorization` substring, so sibling masking does not run (`context.py:169-185`). `_redact_assignments` is called at `context.py:441` and its return value is ignored; only an exception stops the original-text return. On `SyntaxError`, `context.py:679-685` raises only when the expression starts with `$` and contains a call. String addition without a call continues. `context.py:686-689` rechecks a `{?` fragment only when the span is not the whole text (`opening > 0 or closing < len(text)`). The pure bracketed record is the whole text, so that check does not run. `redact` then returns the original bytes. A JSON string of that record follows the same path: `cleaned == decoded`, no decoded span is recorded, and the wrapper is preserved.

This violates route-readiness constant-string-addition, bracketed-record, and unresolved-computed-record rules, the concatenated-label rejection, presidential requirements 2, 3, and 5, and EC-ROUTE-4. The round-19 response says dollar-prefixed computed explicit keys reject before effects. The glued and bracketed addition forms still reach the judge.

Minimum repair: when an explicit key or a `{?` key fails to parse, or its text contains string addition or a call that does not resolve to a non-credential literal, reject before any effect. Apply that rejection when the record is the entire document, when `$` or `@` is glued to the quote, and when prose, a JSON string, or backticks wrap it. Keep the existing `$str(...)` rejection, the `str()` addition rejection, and public `Content-Type` text. Do not execute supplied code.
